title: The Bow Hero’s Counterattack
text: “Ren! What do you mean by that?!”
Itsuki is furious after hearing Ren’s words. Well, Ren did get angry when he was lumped in with Itsuki.
“Hmph. I just feel sick being compared to a guy who got completely fooled.”

“And what does that have to do with teamwork?! Anyway, coming from someone who got completely overwhelmed by just one of Naofumi’s allies, saying that’s the ‘right’ way to fight has absolutely no credibility. Aren’t you actually just all talk and no action?”
“What did you say?!”
“What’s that supposed to mean?!”
“I think you’re right.”
Ren and Itsuki began glaring at their Father. They sure are a busy bunch, always fighting or glaring at each other. Eventually, meeting their glares head-on, their Father began to speak.
“I don’t have any experience with games similar to this world, but I’m quite experienced with online games. I’ve met people just like you before.”
Come to think of it, he’d mentioned that before. Actually, there were times when I, too, wondered if Ren had been playing online games all by himself.

“Typical solo players can’t work with others. Above all, they act selfishly and end up blaming others for their failures. Ren looks just like those self-centered solo players… plus, he’s always trying to be alone.”
“It’s not that he likes being alone—he’s the type who ends up alone.”
“Hmph, that’s just how it looks to you.”
“Let me tell you about something a player like you would definitely have done.”
My father paused for a moment, then began speaking while gazing at Ren with a look of pity.

“There was this player who wanted to take on a certain boss. Apparently, he forced a junior guild member to come with him to a high-level hunting ground. What he did was use the junior as bait to ensure his own safety as the main damage dealer… They ended up getting wiped out, but he actually blamed the junior’s death on a lack of preparation, you know? He said, ‘If that junior had prepared properly, I could’ve taken down the boss.’”
Ren’s eyebrows shot up at Father’s words. Does this ring a bell?
“In the end, that player asked for help from me and other top-tier players in a guild he knew, and they managed to defeat the boss. But his demands for a share of the loot were outrageous.”

My Father says this with a look of disgust. I’ve heard rumors about that, too. After all, while I did run a guild myself, I left the management to others and just played with friends for fun. Stories based on actual experience are really valuable.
“‘I landed the first hit, so give me a bigger cut,’ or ‘I’d already weakened it, so give me one of the rare drops,’ or ‘I’m this strong, so make me an officer.’”
“W-well, there sure are some selfish people out there. Are you implying that’s me?”
“If you don’t recognize yourself in that, then fine. If you haven’t caused that much trouble, I’ll apologize.”
There’s no need for you to apologize, Father. I’m sure Ren is the type who does things like that without even realizing it.

“It was way harder to make up for what he did to the juniors. He’d instilled weird habits and knowledge in them. And once those juniors grew up, they’d take on juniors of their own and do the exact same thing. It was a real pain. To top it off, he’d claim he was training and providing combat power…”
“Enough already—stop talking about some crazy guy from a different game. This is a different situation.”

“Ren, you can’t expect strangers to anticipate your coordination just because you assume they know what you’re doing. That’s true no matter the situation. My teammates were just fighting exactly as Ren ordered, so I don’t get why you’re saying that’s wrong.”
“Even so, what’s up with that Wyndia guy! He’s got it out for me!”
Ren slams his fist on the table in frustration and points at my Father.
“Naofumi! Are you actually teaching your companions proper manners!?”
“……I am teaching them. In fact, they’re usually quite well-behaved. But Renz, there’s some history between Wyndia and you… She was trying her best to hold back, too.”
“Huh!?”
“You see… Renz, she was the adopted daughter of the dragon you killed in Melromarc—the one who raised her with great care.”

My father began explaining the Assistant’s background to Ren. He recounted how, thanks to the dragon Ren had killed, the village had become a tourist destination; how adventurers flocked to the dragon’s lair in search of the treasure it had amassed; and how the people who were practically family to the Assistant were killed one after another. He also explained how my father had rescued her just as she was about to be sold into slavery and brought her into the group as a comrade. He even went on to describe what happened to the village afterward. When he first heard this, Ren’s eyes darted around nervously, but he quickly returned to his original look of disgust.
“That’s a classic tear-jerker. How much of this is made up?”
“Itsuki, could you just shut up for a second? That might have been the case with the ‘weakling’ who deceived you, but this is the truth.”
“What kind of way is that to talk!”
“I don’t think it’s a lie, you know? There’s no doubt that Itsuki was deceived like that by the Three Heroes Church.”
“Kuh…!”

Itsuki is being blatantly annoying. Ever since he started arguing back, he’s been saying the same thing over and over. How long does he plan to keep making these lame excuses, insisting he’s not at fault?
“So, to Wyndia-chan, Ren, you’re the one who killed her father and brother. I’ll apologize on her behalf—won’t you forgive her?”
“No wonder she’s abnormally strong. She’s got the power of a dragon inside her. That’s why she’s so strong. She’s using a cheat that’s outside the game’s rules!”
“Wait, ‘outside the rules’… This isn’t a video game, you know…”
“Otherwise, there’s no way to explain it.”
“Just so you know, as Wyndia-chan explained herself, she’s a rear guard… a mage, so to speak. Actually, she’s the least suited for physical combat among us. She hasn’t even had any training in it.”
“That’s exactly right. She’s way worse at close-quarters combat than Keel or Sakura-chan!”
“Motoyasu-kun… ‘weak’…”

Did I say something wrong? The proper way for an Assistant to fight is to provide backup and cast offensive spells from the rear. Isn’t creating situations where she can shine part of what being in a party is all about? Of course, just as an Assistant isn’t suited for the front lines, Keel is a total noob when it comes to Magic.
“Getting punched by a rear-guard Magic user and ending up in the infirmary… So Ren-san really was all talk after all.”
“That’s why I’ve been saying she’s exceptionally strong among Naofumi’s companions!”
“I’m telling you that’s not true. Sure, her upbringing is unusual, but she’s just an ordinary girl.”

“I’m not exactly taking Naofumi’s side here, but Ren-san is, after all, the one who killed her parents, so she can’t really complain about getting punched, can she? And leaving a dragon’s corpse lying around to spread a plague… she’s quite the mass murderer, isn’t she? It’s no wonder people resent her. That is, if that story is true.”

“Hmph, I should’ve just killed both of them—mother and daughter. Then she wouldn’t have done such selfish things and could’ve gone to the afterlife with her parents. Anyway, disposing of corpses isn’t my responsibility. I couldn’t care less.”

Hearing those words, my father flew into a rage and stood up. I recognize that look in his eyes. It’s even sharper than when it was Kou’s turn… It’s similar to the expression he showed in the last loop when Sakura-chan was almost poisoned by Siltvelt. Oh… Father’s gaze is so sharp it sends shivers down my spine.
“Spear Hero… that look is unsettling, so please stop making that face.”
My Finacée called him out on it. Isn’t this guy a bit too harsh on me?

Still, I heard that Ren from the first world felt responsible for the plague. In fact, he seemed to deeply regret killing his Rival. I recall someone saying that was the reason he was traveling with his Assistant.

…What caused Ren to change? I thought the Spirit Tortoise was to blame, but at this rate, he doesn’t seem likely to show any remorse. Is it because—even though the villagers stricken by the plague didn’t harm him—his Assistant actually hit him? Or perhaps it was a case of tit-for-tat, and he just couldn’t back down now?
“Ren…! I thought you were cool, but I expected you to have the passionate heart of a true hero—it seems I was wrong. You’re nothing but a selfish, cold-blooded scoundrel through and through.”
“Hmph. Anyone who harms me is my enemy. I have no need to feel sympathy for my enemies. If you want, I can send you back to your parents right now.”
Thud! Father slams his fist hard on the table, making it clear he’s displeased. That’s not going to happen, though. His parents have been reincarnated and are right here nearby.
“I’ll never let that happen. No matter what, I’ll protect Wyndia-chan from you. When that time comes, Ren… you’d better be prepared.”
“Hmph!”

Both of them kept their eyes averted, refusing to meet each other’s gaze. Hahaha, Ren wouldn’t be able to scratch Father, would he? In fact, he wouldn’t even need Father to step in—the best he could hope for is getting beaten back by my Assistant. If that happened, it wouldn’t end with just a few punches this time. Well, since he’d just loop back to the beginning if he died, I’d stop him anyway.
